subject.title: [Feature]: Structured Callback Actions and Thread Context Inheritance for Agent Handoffs

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-party structured `sessions_send` or handoff outcome contract for skip/no-reply and announce routing now, or keep this as acceptance coverage for a broader A2A handoff design?
rationale: The remaining work changes agent tool/API semantics and message-delivery behavior across session-state boundaries, so automation cannot choose the public contract shape safely.

options.title: Keep as handoff acceptance work
options.body: Keep this issue open and require the next A2A handoff implementation to cover structured skip/no-reply outcomes plus channel/thread inheritance tests.

options.title: Implement a narrow action field
options.body: Add an additive `sessions_send` action/routing override while preserving current sentinel-token behavior and default routing.

options.title: Fold into broader protocol work
options.body: Move these exact acceptance cases under a canonical handoff protocol issue or PR only after that item is open, viable, and explicit about them.

recommendation.title: Keep as handoff acceptance work
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require the next A2A handoff implementation to cover structured skip/no-reply outcomes plus channel/thread inheritance tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined signal from feature history and the maintainer-visible scoping comment on this handoff surface.
